chunks: Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Shuʿayb al-ʿAqarqūfī, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Those who will be closest to me tomorrow are the ones with the best character and the closest of you to the people.'

key_terms.أَقْرَبُكُمْ: the closest of you (indicating rank or proximity)
key_terms.غَدًا: tomorrow (referring to the Day of Judgment/Hereafter)

ai.seo_question: What determines closeness to the Prophet Muhammad (ṣ) in the Hereafter according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Zuhd*, this hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on *khuluq* (moral character) as the primary metric for spiritual proximity to the Prophet, linking inner virtue with outward social kindness. It reflects the tradition that true piety is manifested not merely in ritual but in one's demeanor and accessibility to the community, a concept central to the Ahl al-Bayt's ethical teachings.
